claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

eu_status.description: The claimant's EU Settlement Scheme status, where relevant.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions.

Let's start with: **Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you asking about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, yes, I'm asking about my son Alex. He's 15 and lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you're asking about your son Alex who is 15 and lives at home with you.

To help determine your eligibility for Child Benefit, I need to ask: **Do you live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Great! And just to confirm: **Are you responsible for Alex's care? This typically means you're providing for his day-to-day needs like food, clothes, and accommodation.**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, absolutely. I look after him every day - provide his meals, buy his clothes, and he lives here with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent. Now I need to ask: **Is Alex currently in full-time education, or has he started any paid work?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's not in full-time education and he doesn't work either.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I need to understand Alex's situation a bit more:

**Can you tell me why Alex is not in full-time education? For example, is he home-schooled, does he have special educational needs, or is there another reason?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's just not in education at the moment - he's not home-schooled or anything like that.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I understand. Just a few more questions to complete the assessment:

**Has Alex ever been in hospital, care, or residential accommodation for an extended period, or is he currently in any of these situations?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nothing like that. He's just been at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. One final question to complete the assessment:

**Do you have settled or pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme, or are you a British citizen, or do you have some other immigration status in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I have pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Since you have pre-settled status, I need to ask one more question:

**Are you currently working, looking for work, studying, or do you have sufficient resources to support yourself financially without claiming benefits like Income Support, income-based Jobseeker's Allowance, Pension Credit or Universal Credit?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm not really sure about my financial resources - I mean, I'm getting by, but I don't know if that counts as having "sufficient resources" in the way you mean it.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I understand - that can be a bit unclear. Let me ask it a different way to help clarify:

**Are you currently receiving any of these benefits: Income Support, income-based Jobseeker's Allowance, Pension Credit, or Universal Credit?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I don't know - I'm not sure whether I'm receiving any of those benefits or not.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's alright. Let me ask a different question that might help:

**Are you currently working in a paid job? And if so, do you work regularly (for example, earning a wage each month)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I don't know if I'm working or not - that's not something I have information about.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I understand. Let me try one more approach:

**Are you currently registered as looking for work with a government-sponsored careers service or jobcentre?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I don't have information about whether I'm registered with any careers service or jobcentre.

## Assessment Summary

I've completed my assessment based on the information you've provided. Unfortunately, **I cannot determine whether you are eligible for Child Benefit for Alex** - your eligibility is **INDETERMINATE**.

### Here's why:

**For Alex:** While the basic conditions for Child Benefit appear to be met - Alex is 15 (under 16), lives with you in the UK, and you're responsible for his care - there's a complicating factor with your immigration status.

Because you have **pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme**, you must meet additional "right to reside" conditions to claim Child Benefit. These include being:
- Working and earning above a certain threshold for at least 3 months, OR
- Looking for work (as a registered jobseeker), OR  
- Having sufficient financial resources to support yourself (typically meaning you're not claiming certain benefits), OR
- Studying with sufficient resources

Since you don't have information about your employment status, benefit receipt, or financial resources, I cannot determine whether you meet these additional requirements.

### What to do next:

To find out if you're eligible, you would need to gather information about:
- Whether you're currently working and your earnings
- What benefits (if any) you're receiving
- Your overall financial situation

You can also contact the Child Benefit Office directly - they can review your specific circumstances and give you a definitive answer.
